I've been developing a new show for halloween 2009.

The basic idea is that as people apporach my front door, a coffin lid will open. A smoke machine and green lighting add to the spooky effect. When the doorbell is pressed. All lights extinguish and a thunderclap plays and strobe light simulates lightening whilst the skeleton in the coffin rises.

This video was a lights out dry run of the system. The strobe does not show up too well on the video but you get the idea....

Custom PC software plays spooky music and controls lights and pneumatics which operate the coffin lid and skeleton.

I set up some fake gravestores, green floodlighting, smoke machine, spooky audio with a pneumatically operated coffin. A sensor detects people approaching and opens the coffin door. Inside is a skeleton illuminated with green light.

Dalek Bob, the love child of a drunken night on eBay needed some motors fitting. Here's the brief journey of how I did it.

The control uses an ESP32-S3. It sets up a wireless access point. You connect your mobile to this then navigate to Bob's home page. From here you can select operating the motors or the sound board. Two people can control Bob: One on motors, one on sound.

Oldham college asked Inclusive Bytes, a none profit tech hub I volunteer at if we could create some physical inputs for their ~$100k CAVE system. This is a multi projector multi wall virtual environment...how could I refuse.

I created an ESP8266 D1 mini based board with 4 pushbutton inputs. A C++ application monitors the switches and reports their status in a JSON packet which is sent to an MQTT broker running on the CAVE pc.

As a proof on concept it worked really well. Moving forwards we can integrate similar units into pyhsical props they can use in virtual training scenarios.

videos.t: Festival Badges That Sync Themselves (No Pairing, No WiFi) | CrowdClock
videos.desc:
Find all the build files at:
https://github.com/Inclusive-Bytes/CrowdClock

CrowdClock – badges that synchronise just by being near each other.

These LED badges were built for the Oldham Illuminate Festival 2026 with young people at Inclusive Bytes, a non-profit tech hub focused on hands-on learning and community engagement.

There’s no pairing.
No configuration.
No central controller.

Each badge simply shares its sense of time with nearby badges.
If it sees a newer time, it adopts it — and because every badge runs the same code, they all fall into sync automatically.
